posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
Hi all

I now have my Coherent C315m working. I have also got it mounted on a nice adjustable mount along with my spatial filter. At the moment I don't have the space or stability (i'm working in the garden shed!) to make anything other than simple reflection holograms. I'm hoping that this will change in the not too distant future 

I'm using the same pinhole as I was using previously for the HeNe laser but I realise that it's almost certainly too big a hole as i'm having difficulty getting a perfectly clean beam spread. What size pinhole do you guys use?

I've also just nicely received a box of BB520 plates from Manuel at Colourholographic. I don't want to waste too many plates experimenting with exposure times, so I would be grateful if someone would assist me by passing on their experience with regard to the exposure time required for these plates. I guess probably around the 10 to 15 second mark would perhaps do it. Any thoughts?

Any assistance is greatly appreciated.

Cheers

Jem

posts.author: floh
posts.content_md:
without measuring or experiments we cannot say how long your shot should be. From a friend who use the red sensitive BB plates I know you will get a result even if the exposure is bad. So your first shot should be a hologram. 

What you can do is wasting just one plate that lies on a black paper and another one is on top giving only a small slit of the plate. then shot one second move the top paper shot one second more and so on. After developping you should be able to see which one is the best. Keep in mind the object light which is nearly absent in this experiment would also do exposure so take the second or third best time from experiment.

posts.author: Jem
posts.content_md:
O.K. so, if my calculations are correct (long, long time since I was at school) I reckon I need a round a 6um (ish) pinhole when using a 40x microscope objective. Beam diameter of the C315m is apparently 1.1mm.

If anyone would be prepared to confirm this i'd be most grateful 

Also, I have mounted my spatial filter about 3 inches away from the laser output window on the C315m and aligned it perfectly using my existing 10um pinhole (which I think is a bit too big as some scatter is getting through). I notice that there is some (diffused) back reflection on the output window of the laser, this is obviously coming from the back surface of the objective lens. Do you think that this will be sufficient to damage the laser? Did I ought to move the spatial filter further away thus increasing the diameter of the reflection and therefore lessening the power.

Any opinions please.

Cheers

Jem

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I like to put the spatial filter farther away and pass the beam through a iris to help block stray light. This can be quite a problem in laser diodes where the reflection can cause a mode hop when the shutter opens.

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md:
Jem-

You should be able to use your meter to figure exposure times. I don't know if BB520 is the same as BB640, but assuming it is, I use around 450uJ/cm^2 for OD1 exposure for BB640. If you need help figuring out how to use the meter, consult the manual or send me an email.

-Tony
